signal: EX1 resolves / EX2 forms the redirect

head.text: Branch Predictor — direction misprediction (pred_taken=0, actual_taken=1), EX2 redirect (stage 7e: IF/ID/RR/EX1/EX2)

foot.text: EX1 resolves actual_taken=1 against a not-taken prediction at tick 3 (branch in rr_ex1_q); the mismatch folds into ex1_ex2_q.fault.bpred_dir_mispredict at the EX1->EX2 edge, live at tick 4. ex_redirect_d reads that bit combinationally the same cycle (tick 4) — but kronos_hazard drives its flushes from the REGISTERED ex_redirect_q (kronos_top.sv:958), not ex_redirect_d, so if_id_q/id_rr_q/rr_ex1_q flush and pc_q redirects to T one cycle later, at tick 5. The mispredicting branch itself, already past EX1/EX2, continues to retire normally (ex1_ex2_q.valid pulses once for it at tick 4); only the wrong-path follower that would otherwise land in ex1_ex2_q is squashed. Measured at stage 7e (bench_mispredict vs. bench_taken_branch, §11): a misprediction measures 3 cycles/op more than a correctly-predicted taken branch (15 vs. 12) — both numbers include ~3 cycles/op of shared loop scaffolding (see §11's caption), so 3 is the honest marginal misprediction cost, not either row's absolute value.
